title: Apart from fertility, offspring of crossed species and crossed varieties are alike

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Apart from fertility, offspring of crossed species and crossed varieties are alike

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Apart from fertility, the offspring of crossed species and of crossed varieties are closely similar in their variability, prepotency, reversion and resemblance to their parents.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Laying aside the question of fertility and sterility, in all other respects there seems to be a general and close similarity in the offspring of crossed species, and of crossed varieties.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Hybrids and mongrels compared independently of their fertility”. Scope: hybrids between species and mongrels between varieties, in plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Several components can be compared with existing genetic crosses, but the composite assertion requires substantial harmonization. Broad plant-and-animal coverage is inadequate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Using matched crosses, compare hybrids and within-species variety crosses for phenotypic variance, parental resemblance, transmission distortion or prepotency, and reversion. Similar effect-size distributions after excluding fertility support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched species and variety crosses are uncommon.

Prepotency and reversion lack uniform modern metrics.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.44
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A few model systems have both kinds of cross and could be compared on variance and resemblance, which is a partial test. The open databases do not code prepotency or reversion, so those parts of the list still sit in narrative breeding records. Matched designs are uncommon, and feasibility is closer to months of harmonization than to a ready analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Holding fertility aside, compare interspecific hybrids and intraspecific mongrels on variance, dominance or prepotency, reversion rate, and parent-offspring resemblance. Similar distributions support the claim; a large, repeatable difference on any of those properties would count against a general close similarity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species and variety crosses are rarely measured with the same traits in the same experiment.

Prepotency and reversion are not standardized fields.

Similarity is a judgment across several phenomena, each of which could differ.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data existence: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.5
